title: Em-dash/vocabulary guard relies on a hand-maintained enumeration of form_copy's public surface
detail: The guard is only as complete as all_strings(); a new form_copy string not added to the list silently escapes the CI-guarded em-dash ban. Verified today 105/105 public strings are listed, so this is future drift, not a present leak.
recommended_fix: Own the list in the source module (e.g. pub fn all_public_strings() in form_copy.gleam) so every new string is automatically guarded, or scan serialized pages like content_test does.

title: CopyVars test fixtures triplicated across the three new reference_checks test files
evidence:
+fn vars() -> form_copy.CopyVars {
+  form_copy.CopyVars(
+    referee_name: "Colm Byrne",
+    referee_first_name: "Colm",
+    applicant_first_name: "Aisling",
+    applicant_full_name: "Aisling O'Brien",
+    employer_name: "Acme Ltd",
+    employment_duration: "3 years",
+    job_title: "Senior Chef",
+    annual_salary: "42,000",
+  )
+}
detail: vars() (8 fields, identical literals) is copied into form_copy_test, form_pages_test and questions_test; open_vars() twice. Adding a CopyVars field means editing all copies; Gleam's compiler catches that, but fixture-value drift is unenforced.
recommended_fix: Extract a shared reference_checks test-fixture module (e.g. server/test/reference_checks/support.gleam) exporting vars()/open_vars() and import it from all three files.
